title: LedgerBase — Reset Ticket #
objective: Request a password reset for your own account, then take over the administrator's account instead — without ever seeing their reset link.

verifier.condition: A password reset completes for the 'admin' account using a reset token the attacker was never issued.

weakness: Password reset tokens are issued as short, sequential numbers instead of unpredictable random values, so a token for one account lets you infer a nearby token for another.
vulnerableEndpoint: POST /reset-password/:token (tokens are sequential, issued in request order)
seededData: Users alice and admin. A reset request for admin was made shortly before the instance started, so an in-range token already exists. In-memory.

credentials.label: User account
credentials.note: Request your own reset first to see the token format.

hints: Request a reset for your own account and look closely at the token in the link you get back. Does it look random?
If tokens are issued in order, what would the token right before or after yours belong to?
You don't need admin's email to use their reset link — only their token.
burpNotes: Request a reset for yourself and note the token's format and length. Then try nearby values directly against /reset-password/:token in Repeater.
